L10: ## Immuvera Therapeutics and OMICA Biomed Strengthen Collaboration in Veterinary Oncology
L11: #### Immuvera Therapeutics (Norway) and OMICA Biomed (Spain) are pleased to highlight their growing collaboration in veterinary oncology. Together, the companies are combining Nebumet, Immuvera’s inhaled immunotherapy platform, with OmiCare AI, OMICA’s liquid biopsy and AI-based monitoring solution.
L12: 
L13: 【3†Image†framerusercontent.com】
L14:

L16: 
L17: Immuvera
L18: 
L19: News
L20: 
L21: Apr 10, 2026
L22: 
L23: 1-2 min read
L24: Nebumet is being developed to help prevent and treat lung metastases in dogs, while OmiCare AI is designed to support treatment monitoring through minimally invasive blood testing. The collaboration brings together therapeutic innovation and data-driven disease monitoring with the ambition of improving clinical decision-making, treatment follow-up, and quality of life for dogs with cancer.

L10: ## Successful capital raise paves the way for pet cancer treatment
L11: #### Norwegian biotech company Immuvera Therapeutics has successfully raised capital via Folkeinvest. The company is now preparing for the final stage ahead of the market launch of an innovative medicine to combat cancer in pets.
L12: 
L13: 【3†Image†framerusercontent.com】
L14: 
L15: Written by
L16: 
L17: Immuvera
L18: 
L19: Insight
L20: 
L21: Jan 15, 2026
L22: 
L23: 1-2 min read
L24: Immuvera Therapeutics is developing a new drug to treat cancer in the lungs, a highly burdensome form of cancer with a fatal outcome. The company’s first product is based on the BCG vaccine, which is currently used to treat bladder cancer in humans. Immuvera Therapeutics has adapted the vaccine for use in the lungs and for veterinary medicine, initially in dogs. The dog’s lung tissue is treated locally, stimulating the immune system to attack cancer cells.

L8: # Our Solution
L9: 
L10: Market Opportunity
L11: ## A One Health Opportunity
L12: 
L13: Cancer is one of the leading causes of death in dogs, and owners increasingly seek the same standard of care they would expect for a family member. Yet treatment options remain limited: surgery, chemotherapy and radiation are costly, not widely available, and rarely control cancer once it has spread.
L14: The same is true in people. Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and the lungs are a common site of metastasis. A therapy proven against lung metastases in dogs therefore addresses an unmet need in two species, through one programme.
L15: Market demand is growing rapidly as Millennials and Gen Z, now major pet owners, drive pet humanization and demand for advanced care, with pet insurance seeing significant growth now covering cancer therapy. However, pet parents face very limited treatment options relying on toxic, outdated chemotherapies as veterinary oncology remains decades behind human medicine.
